title: Bought for ₹1,850, sold for ₹2,405
statement: An article bought for ₹1,850 is sold for ₹2,405. What is the profit or loss percentage?
explanation:
Profit = |2,405 − 1,850| = ₹555. Profit and loss percentages are always on the **cost price**:
555 / 1,850 × 100 = **30% profit**.

title: Cost price from ₹3,500 at 25% profit
statement: By selling a watch for ₹3,500, a shopkeeper makes a 25% profit. What did the watch cost him?
explanation:
SP = CP × 125/100, so CP = SP × 100/125 = 3,500 × 100/125 = **₹2,800**.
(Taking 25% of the *selling* price gives ₹2,625 — percentages are on cost.)

title: 12% off a marked price of ₹2,600
statement: A jacket is marked at ₹2,600 and sold at a 12% discount. What is the selling price?
explanation: Discount is on the marked price: 2,600 × 12/100 = ₹312. Selling price = 2,600 − 312 = **₹2,288**.

title: Marked 75% above cost, 25% discount
statement: A shopkeeper marks his goods 75% above the cost price and then allows a discount of 25% on the marked price. What is his profit or loss percentage?
explanation:
Take CP = 100. Marked price = 175. After a 25% discount: 175 × 75/100 = 131.25.
Result on a cost of 100: **31.25% profit**. (Subtracting 75 − 25 ignores that the discount is taken on the larger marked price.)

title: Discounts of 25% and 15% in a row
statement: A store offers successive discounts of 25% and 15%. What single discount is equivalent to these two?
explanation:
After both discounts a ₹100 item costs 100 × 0.75 × 0.85 = 63.75.
Single equivalent discount = 100 − 63.75 = **36.25%**  (formula: d1 + d2 − d1·d2/100).

title: Two items at ₹3,720: 25% gain and 25% loss
statement: Two cycles are sold for ₹3,720 each. On one the seller gains 25% and on the other he loses 25%. What is his overall gain or loss percentage?
explanation:
Costs: 3,720 × 100/125 = 2,976 and 3,720 × 100/75 = 4,960; total cost 7,936 vs revenue 7,440.
Equal selling prices with equal gain% and loss% always give a loss of x²/100 = 25²/100 = **6.25%**.

title: Buy 10 for ₹20, sell 8 for ₹20
statement: A vendor buys bananas at 10 for ₹20 and sells them at 8 for ₹20. What is his profit percentage?
explanation:
CP of one = 20/10, SP of one = 20/8. Profit % = (SP − CP)/CP × 100 = (10 − 8)/8 × 100 = **25%**.
(Dividing by 10 instead of 8 measures the profit on the selling price — a common slip.)

title: Mark-up for 10% profit after a 20% discount
statement: A trader wants a 10% profit even after giving a 20% discount. By what percentage above the cost price should he mark his goods?
explanation:
Take CP = 100, so the required SP = 110. That is 80% of the marked price: MP = 110 × 100/80 = 137.5.
Mark-up = **37.5%** above cost. (Adding 10 + 20 = 30% falls short because the discount is taken on the larger marked price.)
